# rwgpu 0.1.0 command line

Every command accepts `--json` and then prints exactly one JSON object on stdout with `rwgpu`, `format`, `command`, `ok`, `errors`, `warnings` and `diagnostics` fields plus the command's own fields. Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` errors or failed checks, `2` bad command line.

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| [`rwgpu new PATH [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-new) | Create a project from the starter template |
| [`rwgpu check [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-check) | Validate every project file without running anything |
| [`rwgpu run [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-run) | Run a scene headless for N frames |
| [`rwgpu shot [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-shot) | Render a frame to PNG, with a text report of what is drawn where |
| [`rwgpu inspect [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-inspect) | Dump the world state at a frame as JSON (or a table) |
| [`rwgpu test [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-test) | Run playtests: scripted input, expectations and reference screenshots |
| [`rwgpu explain [TOPIC] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-explain) | Explain a diagnostic code, a file format/component, or a command |
| [`rwgpu schema [KIND] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-schema) | Print the JSON Schema of a file format |
| [`rwgpu docs [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-docs) | Print the reference docs for this exact rwgpu version |
| [`rwgpu serve [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-serve) | Serve the web player for a project (reloads when files change) |
| [`rwgpu export TARGET [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-export) | Write a project as a folder that any static web host can serve |
| [`rwgpu play [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-play) | Play a project in a window, drawn with the GPU (needs the native player) |
| [`rwgpu help [COMMAND] [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-help) | Show help for rwgpu or a command |
| [`rwgpu version [FLAGS]`](#rwgpu-version) | Print the rwgpu version |

## rwgpu new

```text
rwgpu new — Create a project from the starter template

Usage: rwgpu new PATH [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  PATH         Folder to create (must not exist or be empty).

Flags:
  --name NAME        Project name (default: the folder name).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Writes rwgpu.toml, a starter scene, prefabs, a playtest and an AGENTS.md generated for this rwgpu version, then checks the result.

Examples:
  rwgpu new my-game
  rwgpu new games/maze --name "Maze"
```

## rwgpu check

```text
rwgpu check — Validate every project file without running anything

Usage: rwgpu check [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Parses rwgpu.toml, every scene, prefab and playtest; checks types, unknown keys, references between files and static problems (overlapping solids, signals that can never fire). Exit code 1 if there are errors; warnings do not fail.

Examples:
  rwgpu check
  rwgpu check my-game --json
```

## rwgpu run

```text
rwgpu run — Run a scene headless for N frames

Usage: rwgpu run [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --frames N         Frames (fixed steps) to run. Default: the playtest's frames, else 300.
  --input FILE       Drive the scene with a playtest's [[input]] (and use its scene and seed).
  --seed N           Override the random seed.
  --events           Include the event log.
  --watch NAMES      Write every event of these, however many happen: entity names or #ID, event kinds (moved, blocked, trigger), or `all`; comma-separated. Past 256 events of one of those kinds in a step, the others are counted, not written.
  --hash-every N     Record the state hash every N frames (to find where two runs diverge).
  --track NAME       Print the cells an entity occupies, with frame ranges (timing puzzles, patrols).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Deterministic: the same files, input and seed always give the same state hash, on every platform. No window and no GPU are used. In a step with more than 256 `moved`, `blocked`, `trigger` or `custom` events (a large world), the first 256 of each kind are written, the others counted, and an `omitted` event says how many; `--watch NAME` writes all of an entity's. A step that reaches a limit on work (`rwgpu explain limits`) is reported with the limit's code.

Examples:
  rwgpu run --frames 300
  rwgpu run tests/walkthrough.toml --events
  rwgpu run --frames 38 --watch walker_17 --events
  rwgpu run --frames 120 --track guard
  rwgpu run scenes/garden.toml --input tests/walkthrough.toml --json
```

## rwgpu shot

```text
rwgpu shot — Render a frame to PNG, with a text report of what is drawn where

Usage: rwgpu shot [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --frame N          Frame to render. Default: the playtest's last frame, else 0.
  --input FILE       Drive the scene with a playtest's [[input]] (and use its scene and seed).
  --seed N           Override the random seed.
  --out FILE         PNG path. Default: out/<scene>_f<frame>.png in the project.
  --compare FILE     Compare with a reference PNG; exit 1 if it differs (writes <out>.diff.png).
  --max-diff N       With --compare: pixels allowed to differ (default 0).
  --report           Print the frame report (always included with --json).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

The picture is drawn by a deterministic CPU renderer, in 3D, from the camera as it is at that frame: identical pixels on every machine. The frame report lists each entity's screen rectangle, visible pixels and what covers it, and flags off-screen (W0301), hidden (W0302) and clipped (W0303) entities.

Examples:
  rwgpu shot
  rwgpu shot --input tests/walkthrough.toml --report
  rwgpu shot --frame 120 --out a.png --json
```

## rwgpu inspect

```text
rwgpu inspect — Dump the world state at a frame as JSON (or a table)

Usage: rwgpu inspect [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --frame N          Frame to inspect. Default: the playtest's last frame, else 0.
  --input FILE       Drive the scene with a playtest's [[input]] (and use its scene and seed).
  --seed N           Override the random seed.
  --entity NAME      Only this entity (and, with --events, its events, every one of them written).
  --component NAME   Only entities with this component (sprite, trigger, ...).
  --events           Include the event log: what happened and what was refused, and why.
  --since N          With --events: only events from frame N on.
  --watch NAMES      Write every event of these, however many happen: entity names or #ID, event kinds (moved, blocked, trigger), or `all`; comma-separated. Past 256 events of one of those kinds in a step, the others are counted, not written.
  --place PREFAB[@X,Y] Can I build here? With a cell: whether a `spawn` of PREFAB fits there at this frame, and why not. Without: every cell where it fits. Prints only that answer (add --entity for the table).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Answers what exists, where it is, and why something happened. The text table is a summary (cell, components, solid, cooldown, patrol target, screen rectangle, tap point); --json has every component and all runtime state, plus `ground` (size, and the map and terrain legend for terrain maps). `tap` is a pixel where a tap is guaranteed to hit the entity. `--place` applies the same rules as the `spawn` action (inside the ground, buildable terrain, nothing enabled standing there).

Examples:
  rwgpu inspect --json
  rwgpu inspect --input tests/walkthrough.toml --frame 60 --entity player --events
  rwgpu inspect --input tests/build.toml --frame 120 --place house@3,2
```

## rwgpu test

```text
rwgpu test — Run playtests: scripted input, expectations and reference screenshots

Usage: rwgpu test [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder or a single playtest file (default: current folder).

Flags:
  --filter TEXT      Only playtests whose name contains TEXT.
  --update-refs      Write reference images from the current output instead of comparing.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Runs every tests/*.toml. Failed expectations are E0401 with the entity's recent events; image mismatches are E0402 and write the actual and diff images under out/tests/.

Examples:
  rwgpu test
  rwgpu test --filter walk --json
  rwgpu test --update-refs
```

## rwgpu explain

```text
rwgpu explain — Explain a diagnostic code, a file format/component, or a command

Usage: rwgpu explain [TOPIC] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [TOPIC]      A code (E0103), a component or format (sprite, entity, connect, playtest) or a command. Omit to list topics.

Flags:
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Like `rustc --explain`, for rwgpu's codes and file formats.

Examples:
  rwgpu explain
  rwgpu explain E0201
  rwgpu explain sprite
  rwgpu explain trigger --json
```

## rwgpu schema

```text
rwgpu schema — Print the JSON Schema of a file format

Usage: rwgpu schema [KIND] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [KIND]       project, scene, prefab or playtest. Omit to list them.

Flags:
  --out DIR          Write all schemas into DIR as <kind>.schema.json.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Editors (e.g. VS Code + Even Better TOML) can use these for completion and inline errors.

Examples:
  rwgpu schema scene
  rwgpu schema --out .rwgpu/schema
```

## rwgpu docs

```text
rwgpu docs — Print the reference docs for this exact rwgpu version

Usage: rwgpu docs [FLAGS]

Flags:
  --agents           Print the AGENTS.md that `rwgpu new` writes into projects.
  --out DIR          Write cli.md, formats.md, errors.md and schemas/ into DIR.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Docs are generated from the same registries the engine uses, so they always match the installed version.

Examples:
  rwgpu docs
  rwgpu docs --agents > AGENTS.md
```

## rwgpu serve

```text
rwgpu serve — Serve the web player for a project (reloads when files change)

Usage: rwgpu serve [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --port N           Port on 127.0.0.1 (default 4410; 0 picks a free one and prints it).
  --web-player DIR   The WebGPU player's folder, as `cargo xtask web-player` writes it. Default: RWGPU_WEB_PLAYER, else `web-player` next to rwgpu, else (from the source tree) target/web-player.
  --wasm FILE        The CPU player's module, rwgpuengine_web.wasm, instead of the WebGPU player. Default, when no WebGPU player is found: RWGPU_WEB_WASM, else next to rwgpu, else (from the source tree) where `cargo xtask web` writes it.
  --site DIR         Serve a folder as it is, as a static web host would (a folder made by `rwgpu export web`), instead of a project.

Opens nothing by itself; visit the printed URL, and its first line says which player it serves and from where. rwgpu itself never needs a GPU: it only serves files. The project's files are read again on every request, and the page reloads when they change. URL parameters: scene=PATH, input=PATH, frames=N (run N frames immediately, then pause), renderer=cpu (draw with the CPU reference renderer). The page shows the frame number and state hash, which match `rwgpu run` for the same input.

The WebGPU player has the bindings of `rwgpu play` (see `rwgpu help play`): keys, taps, swipes and the camera, with a two-finger pinch on a touch screen. The CPU player has keys, taps and swipes.

--site DIR serves a folder as it is, as a static web host would: one made by `rwgpu export web`.

The web player is the WebGPU player when one is found (ADR 0024): the frame is drawn with WebGPU where the browser has it and by the CPU reference renderer where it has not, and the page says which in one line. Otherwise it is the CPU player (rwgpuengine_web.wasm). A flag names the one place and beats a variable: --web-player, --wasm, then RWGPU_WEB_PLAYER, RWGPU_WEB_WASM. With none, `web-player` next to rwgpu, then (from the source tree) target/web-player, then rwgpuengine_web.wasm in the same two places. E0008 when none is found; `cargo xtask dist` puts both players next to the release rwgpu.

Examples:
  rwgpu serve examples/tiny_town
  rwgpu serve --port 8080
  rwgpu serve examples/iso_garden --wasm target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/web/rwgpuengine_web.wasm
  rwgpu serve --site out/web
```

## rwgpu export

```text
rwgpu export — Write a project as a folder that any static web host can serve

Usage: rwgpu export TARGET [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  TARGET       What to make. `web` is the one target: a folder with the page, the web player and the game.
  [PATH]       Project folder, or a file in it (default: current folder).

Flags:
  --out DIR          The folder to write (needed). It must be new or empty, unless --force.
  --force            Write into a folder that is not empty: the export's own files are replaced, nothing else is changed or deleted (W0001 names what else is there).
  --web-player DIR   The WebGPU player's folder, as `cargo xtask web-player` writes it. Default: RWGPU_WEB_PLAYER, else `web-player` next to rwgpu, else (from the source tree) target/web-player.
  --wasm FILE        The CPU player's module, rwgpuengine_web.wasm, instead of the WebGPU player. Default, when no WebGPU player is found: RWGPU_WEB_WASM, else next to rwgpu, else (from the source tree) where `cargo xtask web` writes it.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Checks the project first: one that does not pass `rwgpu check` is not exported, and the diagnostics are the checker's. Then writes the player's files, the game's lists (project.json) and the game's files as one bundle (bundle.txt): the files `rwgpu serve` serves, written once. The WebGPU player is index.html, player.js, rwgpu_web.js and rwgpu_web_bg.wasm, copied as they are; the CPU player is index.html, player.js and player.wasm. The bundle holds rwgpu.toml, scenes/, prefabs/ and tests/ (and the main scene and playtests' scenes wherever they are); reference pictures, notes and other files stay behind, and --json lists them and why.

Every address in the folder is relative, so it works at the root of a site and under a path. Any static web host serves it; serving .wasm as application/wasm lets the browser compile the module while it downloads. It needs a web server: opened as a file, browsers refuse to load the module. WebGPU needs a secure context (https, or http on localhost); elsewhere the page draws with the CPU. `rwgpu serve --site DIR` serves the folder as a host would. The same project and player give the same bytes, with no time and no path of this machine in them.

--json says which player, and lists each file with its size, its hash (FNV-1a 64) and what it is, the bundled files and why, the files left out, and how to try the folder. E0005 if the folder is not empty (without --force), E0008 if no player is found, E0003 if --out is the project folder or holds it.

The web player is the WebGPU player when one is found (ADR 0024): the frame is drawn with WebGPU where the browser has it and by the CPU reference renderer where it has not, and the page says which in one line. Otherwise it is the CPU player (rwgpuengine_web.wasm). A flag names the one place and beats a variable: --web-player, --wasm, then RWGPU_WEB_PLAYER, RWGPU_WEB_WASM. With none, `web-player` next to rwgpu, then (from the source tree) target/web-player, then rwgpuengine_web.wasm in the same two places. E0008 when none is found; `cargo xtask dist` puts both players next to the release rwgpu.

Examples:
  rwgpu export web --out out/web
  rwgpu export web examples/tiny_town --out site/town --json
  rwgpu export web --out out/web --force
```

## rwgpu play

```text
rwgpu play — Play a project in a window, drawn with the GPU (needs the native player)

Usage: rwgpu play [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to rwgpu.toml.

Flags:
  --input FILE       Drive the scene with a playtest's [[input]] (and use its scene and seed).
  --seed N           Override the random seed.
  --frames N         Close after N frames and print the result. Default: the playtest's frames with --input, else play until the window is closed.
  --headless         No window: take the steps as fast as they go and draw each changed frame off screen. Needs --frames or --input.
  --screenshot FILE  At the end, save what the window shows as a PNG (with --headless, the frame itself).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Starts the native player, `rwgpu-player`, which `rwgpu` looks for next to itself and then on PATH: rwgpu itself never needs a GPU. The player steps the simulation at the project's tick rate whatever the display does, draws with the GPU only when the picture changed, and scales the frame to the window with bars around it. When the window closes it prints the frame and the state hash: with --input they match `rwgpu run` for the same file.

Keys and taps, as in the web player: arrows or W A S D move, Enter or Space confirm, Escape cancel. A click is a tap; a drag of 12 frame pixels or more is a swipe along the iso axes (up-right is up).

Camera: Q and E turn a quarter turn; right-drag turns freely; middle-drag or Shift + right-drag pans; the wheel, a pinch, - and = zoom; V switches between iso and perspective; Home goes back to the scene's camera.

E0006 when the player is not installed: build it from a clone of the repository with `cargo install --locked --path players/rwgpuengine_player`.

Examples:
  rwgpu play examples/tiny_town
  rwgpu play examples/tiny_town --input tests/turn_and_build.toml --screenshot out/turned.png
  rwgpu play tests/build_town.toml --headless --json
```

## rwgpu help

```text
rwgpu help — Show help for rwgpu or a command

Usage: rwgpu help [COMMAND] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [COMMAND]    Command to describe.

Flags:
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

`rwgpu help --json` lists every command, argument and flag as data.

Examples:
  rwgpu help
  rwgpu help shot
  rwgpu help --json
```
